title: Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
seo_title: KL Standard Chartered Marathon 2026 Review | 2025 Edition
meta_description: KLSCM review: the 2025 edition drew 41,000+ runners over 4-5 October, on a hillier, humid route with a new finish at Merdeka Stadium. What to expect in 2026.
dek: Malaysia's biggest mass-participation race drew more than 41,000 runners in October 2025, on a route runners called tougher than before. Here is what that edition was like, and what it tells you about the 2026 race.
verdict: The Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon is Malaysia's big one. The 2025 edition, over 4 and 5 October, drew more than 41,000 runners across six categories, including 12,147 in the full marathon and 13,035 in the half [1]. It was also a hard race. Runners said the 2025 route was more gruelling than in earlier years, with rolling hills and high humidity, and the finish moved from Dataran Merdeka to Merdeka Stadium [1]. The top Malaysian marathoner, Yeow Ni Jia, described the final kilometres as torturous [1]. If you want the biggest race in Malaysia and a strong field, enter. Just don't expect a fast course.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition in Numbers
paragraphs: The 2025 race was held over the weekend of 4 and 5 October and drew more than 41,000 participants across six categories: full marathon (12,147), half marathon (13,035), 10 km (10,870), 5 km (4,527) and two kids' dashes [1].
KLSCM is described as Malaysia's largest mass-participation sporting event [1], and the 2025 turnout shows why.

sections.heading: A Harder Route, and a New Finish
paragraphs: Runners said the 2025 route was more gruelling than in previous years, with rolling hills and higher humidity testing endurance and mental strength [1]. The finish moved from Dataran Merdeka to Merdeka Stadium, which added an unexpected psychological hurdle at the end [1].
Yeow Ni Jia, the top Malaysian man, said the final kilometres felt torturous but ultimately rewarding, and described the new finish as part of the mental challenge [1].

sections.heading: The Front of the Race
paragraphs: Kenyan athletes dominated the overall race [1]. Among Malaysians, Yeow Ni Jia won the full marathon open category in 2:36:13, ahead of Tan Huong Leong (2:37:05) and 2024 champion Muhaizar Mohamad (2:44:37) [1]. Michelle Chua won the Malaysian women's open in 3:05:40, ahead of Noor Amelia Musa and Lee Siok Chin [1].
The Philippines' Sonny Wagdos won the men's 10 km [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big-city marathon atmosphere in Southeast Asia: 41,000 runners, a strong international field and a route through central Kuala Lumpur.

Train for hills and heat. The 2025 route had rolling sections and humidity that runners found harder than before, so aim for a solid run rather than a personal best, and check whether the 2026 course and finish have changed again.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition, including runners' comments. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.
